business_problem: BNP Paribas must design and distribute investment products tailored to each retail customer while handling very large volumes of information, complying with stringent regulation, and giving advisers and customers clear explanations, regular reports, and proactive support despite the growing complexity of investment choices.
solution_summary: BNP Paribas uses a portfolio of in-house AI capabilities across the investment-advisory value chain rather than a single named external platform. The bank applies ongoing analysis of news about issuers of financial securities, including screening negative media coverage, to identify signals that could affect share prices or ESG ratings. It uses tools for portfolio managers to improve fund performance, automates preparation of multilingual performance reports and regulatory or contractual documents, and automates parts of new-customer onboarding to reduce delays and data-entry or analysis errors. For advice generation, an algorithm proposes asset allocations and portfolios using client attributes such as risk profile, financial knowledge, investment purpose, time horizon, and ESG preferences, while natural-language generation creates clear written explanations of proposals. Internal conversational assistants help advisers prepare for customer appointments and answer specific questions, and models identify customers whose investments need adjustment. These capabilities are deployed across BNP Paribas entities in Europe with Group IT and Data support and an as-a-service rollout model.
